# py-ops - Python op layer (jix-py/src/ops/)

Paths are relative to `jix-py/src/` unless they start with `jix/` or `jix-py/python/`.

## Purpose

Turns arbitrary Python inputs (jix `Array`, numpy arrays/scalars, Python bool/int/float/complex,
lists) into `Operand`s, picks a typed Rust kernel at runtime from a per-op dispatch table (casting
operands as needed), broadcasts shapes NumPy-style, and wraps the jix_core lazy ops: element-wise
families under `ops/elementwise/` (same file names as core), reductions (`ops/reduction.rs`),
shape ops and basic indexing (`ops/shape_ops.rs`), `asarray`/`cast`/`dtype_sub_field`. Nothing
here reads array data; results are lazy `Array`s. Shared helpers in `util.rs` (slice_unpack,
normalize_dim*, array_try_map) and `type_hint.rs` (`Dim`, `ItemOrTuple`) are in scope. `out=`
lives in array.rs (py-core), not here.

## Contracts

Operand model (`ops/common/operand.rs:17-26`): `PyArray(Py<Array>)` (a jix Array, keeps its cached
numpy dtype), `Array(ArrayAny)` (numpy data wrapped zero-copy in `Plain`), or `Scalar{value, shape,
precision, params}`. `precision == None` means "untyped Python value".

Python -> Operand (`operand.rs:33-153`): jix Array -> PyArray (params ignored). Python `bool` is
checked before `int` -> `Bool, Some(P1)` (typed on purpose). `int` -> `Int(i64), None`; an int
outside i64 raises OverflowError "out of bounds for int64" (54-58) for EVERY op, even next to a
u64/float array. `float`/`complex` -> untyped. `np.generic` (incl. np.float64, a float subclass)
skips this (48) and goes through `np.asarray`; any 0-d numpy array with a scalar dtype becomes a
TYPED Scalar via `.item()` (88-150; f16 via f32 extract, complex precision = itemsize/2). Anything
else -> `plain_from_numpy` (449-520). `only_scalar` (78-80) is used by `Scalar::from_any`
(322-329) for isclose tolerances: arrays, 0-d ndarrays and jix Arrays raise TypeError.

`plain_from_numpy`: inner-shape branch (456-491) is reachable only from `Array.plain()`
(array.rs:733), because numpy expands sub-array dtypes into dims; `check_ndim` (493); strides of
dims with len <= 1, and all strides of an empty array, are replaced by itemsize (504-505);
negative strides on other dims -> ValueError (507-508); zero strides (np.broadcast_to) and
unaligned data are accepted. Big-endian numpy dtypes are rejected in `dtype_from_numpy`
(dtype.rs:141-146, recursive for struct fields 211).

Cast rules (`ops/common/dtype_promote.rs:61-141`), src = (Rank, Option<Precision>):
- An untyped Int with a UInt target is re-ranked to UInt first (66-72): a Python int fits signed
  and unsigned slots; the VALUE is checked later by `Operand::cast`, not here.
- `None` (75-77): same rank and (untyped or equal precision).
- `Safe` (78-134): never down-rank; Bool -> anything; same rank and Float -> Complex need
  `p <= dst`; UInt -> Int needs `p.higher() <= dst` (u64 -> any int: false); Int/UInt ->
  Float/Complex: `dst == P8` always allowed (lossy i64/u64 -> f64 accepted), else
  `p.higher() <= dst`; untyped always allowed.
- `Unsafe` (135-139): anything except Complex -> UInt/Int/Float.

Dispatch (`ops/common/dispatch.rs:196-258`): every operand needs a plain scalar dtype, else
TypeError "does not support operands with dtypes" (257, 263-302). If ALL operands are untyped
they are set to P8 (Bool P1) for selection only (210, `cast_python_scalars_to_default_precision`
dtype_promote.rs:225-239). If the table has `cast_untyped_float_to_f64` (comparisons, isclose)
and no operand is a typed float/complex, untyped floats/complexes select as P8 (211-220). If no
operand is Float/Complex P2, every descriptor mentioning F16 is skipped (221-233). The first
descriptor whose every input passes its CastKind wins; operands are cast with `Operand::cast`
(249) and a cast error (e.g. OverflowError) is RETURNED, never a fall-through. Table order is
semantics. Operand order in `in_dtypes` == descriptor input order.

`Operand::cast` (`operand.rs:155-188`): untyped Scalars only are range-checked: ints against
integer targets (`check_int_in_bounds` 416-446, i128 compare; float/complex/bool targets never
checked, so `f16_arr + 70000 -> inf`), floats/complex against float/complex targets
(`check_float_in_bounds` 385-414: finite -> inf or nonzero -> 0 raises OverflowError; NaN/inf
pass). Typed scalars are never checked (they are never narrowed under Safe). Scalars are
converted value-wise (`Scalar::cast` 331-383, core `Cast`) and rebuilt at the target precision;
`into_array` (190-260) builds `jix_core::__private::Scalar` storage of exactly that type (no
`Cast<Scalar>` view - pinned by test_type_promotion.py:741-800). PyArray whose dtype already
equals the kind is kept as is (176-184); other arrays go through `cast_impl`
(`ops/elementwise/casting.rs:55-138`: same-itemsize int<->int transmute 63-66, else
`Cast::new_array`; complex -> non-complex/non-bool and struct casts -> TypeError 133-137).
The `into_typed::<T>().unwrap()` calls (dispatch.rs:90, 117-118, 157, 187-188) rely on that cast
producing exactly `T::DTYPE`; macro tables take the descriptor dtype and `into_typed` from the
same `T`, so they are type-consistent by construction (macros.rs:1-201).

Promotion for where/stack/concatenate (`dtype_promote.rs:144-222`): if every operand is an array
and all dtypes are equal (struct dtypes included) -> no cast. Otherwise the first kind in
[Bool,U8,I8,U16,I16,U32,I32,U64,I64,(F16 only with an f16 input),F32,F64,C64,C128] that every
operand Safe-casts to (after the all-untyped P8 default; NO f64 rule for untyped floats); none ->
TypeError. Casts use `Operand::cast`, so untyped Python scalars are range-checked here too.

Broadcasting (`ops/common/broadcast.rs`): `broadcast_shapes` (73-105) right-aligned NumPy rules,
result ndim = max input ndim, failure -> core InvalidShapeOperation -> RuntimeError.
`broadcast_operand` (39-71) returns the operand untouched if its shape matches, a Scalar only gets
its `shape` replaced, arrays go through `broadcast_array_impl` (shape_ops.rs:96-131: InsertDim of
leading dims, then `Broadcast`; also used by `jix.broadcast`). A broadcast PyArray becomes
`Operand::Array` (drops its cached numpy dtype; batch7-5 found this is a defect, not a contract: K180). Call order: define_op2 / multiply / power /
divide / remainder / clamp / isclose / rotate broadcast BEFORE dispatch; `where` broadcasts all
three, then promotes x/y (select.rs:65-66); unary ops and reductions never broadcast.

Error mapping (`util.rs:64-100`): a PyErr in the core error's source chain is re-raised as is;
`Arithmetic` -> ArithmeticError (integer div by zero / negative power, raised at READ time),
`UnsupportedDtype` -> TypeError, `Io` -> OSError, every other core kind -> RuntimeError (e.g.
duplicate dims, broadcast failure, empty max/argmax). Python-side checks raise ValueError /
IndexError / TypeError / OverflowError directly.

Core validates (jix/src/ops/...): reduction dims OOB/dup/empty (reduction/common.rs:122-151);
InsertDim output positions any order, dup, check_ndim (shape_ops/insert_dim.rs:59-80);
PermuteDims (permute_dims.rs:50-67); RemoveDim range/dup/len==1 (remove_dim.rs:60-73); Reshape
(reshape.rs:43-53); Stack/Concatenate (stack.rs:65-96, concatenate.rs:72-119); Broadcast
(broadcast.rs:55-75); Repeat/Tile ndim < NDIM_MAX + checked_mul (repeat.rs:42-64, tile.rs:58-80);
Roll len 0 (roll.rs:51-55); Flip (flip.rs:46-62); Select bool8 cond, same x/y dtype; dims <=
i64::MAX and bytes <= u64 (`check_shape_overflow`, jix/src/error.rs:192-207).

What core panics on (this layer must prevent it): ArrayVec capacity (`DimArray`, cap 8) on
collect/push - bounded by `ItemOrTuple::into_dim_array` (type_hint.rs:202), `normalize_dims`
(util.rs:256), the index tuple guard (shape_ops.rs:248) + `consumers > ndim` (292), insert_dim's
`out_ndim` check (439), `assert!` in broadcast.rs:48; `transmute_elements_dyn` panics on itemsize
mismatch (jix/src/ops/transmute.rs:137) - guarded by casting.rs:63; the `into_typed` unwraps
above; `Precision::from_itemsize` / `scalar_kind_to_rank_precision` `unreachable!` for non-scalar
kinds (dtype_promote.rs:32, operand.rs:307) - callers only pass scalar kinds;
`OpFnDescriptor::new2`'s `items.try_into().unwrap()` (dispatch.rs:124) - macros pass 2-arrays;
`unreachable!` precision arms in `into_array` (219, 245, 254). Python ints: `Dim` is i32 and
rejects bool (type_hint.rs:94-109), repeats u64, shift i64, shape entries i64 - pyo3 raises
OverflowError outside those ranges.

## Unsafe inventory

- operand.rs:512 `&*array.as_array_ptr()` to read `fields.data`: live PyArrayObject held as a
  `Bound` under the GIL. Sound.
- operand.rs:516-518 `Plain::new(array.unbind(), data_ptr, shape, strides, dtype, params)`.
  Contract jix/src/storage/plain.rs:97-108 (alignment NOT required, 85-88): (a) pointer outlives
  storage - the `Py<PyUntypedArray>` is stored as `allocation`, keeping numpy array and base
  alive; (b) every index readable at the given strides - inherited from numpy's own invariant
  (as_strided can break it, as in numpy); (c) unsigned strides - checked 507-508; (d) ndim -
  checked 493. NOT established: no writes while jix reads (Python code, another thread, or an
  `out=` aliasing the input - documented UB, array.rs:486-504, K31 intended); K111 (whole-span
  slices alias interleaved views, open); K152 (free-threaded: ndim/shape/strides read separately
  at 454/495/502, concurrent `.shape=` races, open). Element validity is no longer needed: bools
  are `bool8` (any byte valid).
- util.rs:36 `PySlice_Unpack` FFI and 40-42 deref of `PySliceObject.stop` (non-abi3 build, slice
  objects immutable): live slice, valid out-pointers, error fetched on < 0. Sound.
- util.rs:331-418 `array_try_from_fn` / `array_try_map` (used by broadcast_operands and
  operands_dtype_promotion on `[Operand; N]`, which needs_drop): each src index is `ptr::read`
  once and `DropGuard.next` is advanced before calling `f`, so on Err/panic exactly `src[next..]`
  is dropped and `InitGuard` drops initialized outputs. Reviewed sound; non-local only in that
  callers must not rely on side effects of un-mapped items.
- util.rs:116-202 numpy C-API helpers, 280-294 `UnsafeSend` (unused): py-core. casting.rs:64's
  transmute is safe since #105; no other unsafe in ops/elementwise/, reductions or shape ops.

## Edge-case surface

- Python ints: value vs pick (`u8_arr + 256` / `-1` -> OverflowError; `u64_arr == -1` raises,
  numpy gives False); ints > i64::MAX always raise; Python bool is typed (P1), so `True + 1` is
  not the all-untyped 64-bit case. `bitwise_rotate` casts an untyped int amount to u32 first
  (bitwise.rs:481-490): negative or > u32::MAX amount -> OverflowError.
- Floats: untyped float next to an int/bool picks f32 unless the op has the f64 flag (`i8 + 1.5`
  -> f32, `i8 == 1.5` in f64); next to typed f16/f32 it adopts that dtype, range-checked (`f16 +
  1e5`, `f32 > 1e-50` raise). Int-only inputs to float-only ops get f32 (`sqrt(u8)`, `i8 / i8`),
  32-bit ints and wider f64. f64 -> f16 is `f16::from_f64` (operand.rs:243, 351, 392; K71 open).
- Mixed signed/unsigned: u64 with any signed int -> f64 (lossy above 2**53), except comparisons,
  which have exact (u64,i64)/(i64,u64) kernels (cmp.rs:56, 99, 141, 181, 221, 261) - but those
  pairs come after the u64/i64 slots, so a Python int next to u64 still lands in u64.
- 0-d: numpy 0-d -> typed Scalar (copy); jix 0-d stays PyArray. Reductions/shape ops take any
  input through `asarray`, so Python scalars become 0-d Scalar storage. `dim=None` single-dim
  reductions and repeat/roll/tile require ndim == 1 (util.rs:234-247).
- Reductions: `dim=()` -> reduce nothing; `dim=None` -> all dims; OOB -> ValueError (util.rs:223),
  duplicates -> core RuntimeError; keepdim re-inserts at the normalized (possibly unsorted) input
  positions (reduction.rs:8-24, 71-73, 117-119), valid because InsertDim takes output positions in
  any order.
- Indexing (`parse_basic_index`, shape_ops.rs:228-378, also Array.__getitem__/numpy via
  array.rs:176-211): strict bounds, step must be 1, start == len allowed (empty), Python bool
  rejected (271), `__index__` objects (np ints) accepted; omitted stop -> len (util.rs:39-45), an
  explicit huge stop/start stays PY_SSIZE_T_MAX/MIN and raises. 32-bit: any explicit slice on a
  dim longer than i32::MAX raises IndexError (util.rs:26-30); ints/Ellipsis still work. `as i64`
  dim casts (309, 317, 333, 370) rely on dims <= i64::MAX (core `check_shape_overflow`).
- reshape (711-769): checked `known_size` product; `-1` with known_size 0 raises, zero-size array
  infers 0; `array.shape().iter().product()` (747) relies on validated shapes. flatten of 0-d ->
  (1,).
- NDIM_MAX: stack of 8-d arrays -> core RuntimeError; repeat/tile of an 8-d array raise in core
  unless repeats == 1 (early return 1025, 1213 before the core check); insert_dim checks
  `ndim + len(dim) <= 8` (438-443); permute_dims takes `Vec<Dim>` (any sequence) bounded by
  `normalize_dims`.
- Struct dtypes: only shape ops, cast-to-same, where/stack/concatenate of identical dtypes and
  dtype_sub_field accept them. Aliasing: ops never write; `Array.numpy(out=)` (array.rs:213-308)
  rejects self-overlapping outs but not overlap with inputs (documented UB).

## Intentional behaviors (do not report)

- First matching descriptor wins and a value that does not fit raises instead of trying the
  next: `u8_arr + 256`, `bool_arr + 1000`, `power(int_arr, -1)` raise OverflowError; comparisons,
  maximum, clamp, isclose too (test_type_promotion.py:422-453, 500-509, 719).
- Untyped int fills unsigned slots: `u64 + 1` stays u64, `2 ** u8_arr` is u8 (481-498, 698).
- Typed numpy scalar out of range promotes (511-517); Python int outside i64 always raises
  (520-529); Python int into a float slot is unchecked (531-534); out-of-range Python FLOAT raises
  (407-419; K125). Python bool typed: `True + 1 -> u8` (365-373). All-untyped -> 64-bit (358-362).
  Comparisons/isclose with an untyped float run in f64 (383-404; K113). No f16 input -> never f16
  (595-610); an f16 operand keeps f16 (613-618).
- `negative(uN) -> iN` wrapping, `negative(bool) -> i8` (arith.rs:25-28; test_arith.py:201-231).
  `bool + bool -> u8`, `bool - bool -> i8` (arith.rs:251, 307-308; test_arith.py:665-673).
- absolute of uint/bool, floor/ceil/round of ints, real of non-complex, byteswap of 1-byte/bool,
  `clamp(x)` and shape-op no-ops return the input object/scalar as is (arith.rs:81-82,
  rounding.rs:8; test_arith.py:101-109). `+bool` raises (test_arith.py:219-221).
- Power: u64 exponent -> f64 (K65; test_type_promotion.py:679); complex power unsupported (733);
  scalar `** 2` / `** 0.5` use Square/Sqrt with tables mirroring Pow, so dtypes match but
  `-inf ** 0.5 = nan`, `-0.0 ** 0.5 = -0.0`, no float overflow report (K60; test_arith.py:568-700).
  `multiply(a, a)` (same object) goes to square (arith.rs:385-393).
- Integer errors raise ArithmeticError when read; float ops never raise or warn (K126, K145;
  test_arithmetic_errors.py:1-5). divide modes and their numpy deviations: div_rem.rs:9-75, 110-161.
- `where` needs a bool condition (select.rs:9-10); scalar condition or `x is y` returns the
  selected operand itself after broadcast/promotion (17-18; test_select.py:48-66).
- isclose uses `|a-b| <= max(atol, rtol*max(|a|,|b|))`, not numpy's formula, and has no default
  tolerances (cmp.rs:267-276, 329). Shifts by >= width or negative give 0 (bitwise.rs:298-299;
  test_bitwise.py:178). rotate: value never cast, amount Safe-cast to u32, Python int value ->
  i64 (bitwise.rs:374-380; test_bitwise.py:248-265).
- `sum(bool) -> u64`, `product(bool)` unsupported, argmax/argmin -> u64, mean of ints -> f64,
  empty max/argmax/mean/var raise RuntimeError (reduction.rs docs 131-134, 225-226, 284-288,
  319-324, 354-358).
- Slicing strict, step 1, huge bounds raise (shape_ops.rs:144-146; test_slice.py:236-257).
  broadcast() may add leading dims, `-1` keeps an existing dim (17-21). dims accept an int or a
  TUPLE only (test_bad_input.py:88-111); permute_dims takes any sequence. Duplicate dims ->
  RuntimeError (test_shape_ops.py:287-290). repeat/tile with 0 give empty (578, 782).
- asarray ignores `params` for a jix Array (as_array.rs:86-88); `dtype=` for a non-array value
  goes through `numpy.asarray(value, dtype=)` (numpy range checks, K96); numpy scalars use jix's
  Cast (K129).
- `out=` overlapping an input is documented UB (array.rs:486-504; K31).
